sports.h3: Hurkacz knocks Djokovic out of Shanghai Masters
sports.summary: Hubert Hurkacz beat Novak Djokovic 6-4, 6-3 in the second round in Shanghai, while top seed Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton moved through.
body: The 2023 Shanghai champion needed only 87 minutes to beat Djokovic on Friday. It was the Pole's first win over the Serbian after losing all eight of their earlier meetings.

Zverev, the top seed with world number one Jannik Sinner absent through a knee injury, got past Chinese wild card Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (4). Shelton marked his 24th birthday with a 6-3, 7-6 (6) win over Daniel Altmaier.

sports.h3: Alcaraz defends Tokyo title, opens Shanghai bid today
sports.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (4), 6-4 in the Japan Open final, his first title since a four-month wrist layoff.
body: The top seed and defending champion had to work hard against world number 19 Lehecka in Tuesday's final. It was his third title of 2026, including the Australian Open, and the 27th of his career.
Alcaraz had a first-round bye in Shanghai as second seed. He starts his campaign on Saturday against Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerundolo, who beat Nicolas Mejia to set up the meeting.

sports.h3: Mertens stuns Swiatek to reach Beijing semis
sports.summary: Elise Mertens beat Iga Swiatek 7-6 (0), 6-3 at the China Open and will face home favourite Zheng Qinwen next.
body: The Belgian won the first-set tiebreak without dropping a point and broke Swiatek in the second to close it out on Friday. The WTA noted it was her third straight win over a Grand Slam champion.
Zheng reached the last four by beating sixth seed Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6 (6). The other semi-final pits Mirra Andreeva against Nikola Bartunkova.

sports.h3: Verstappen takes Singapore Sprint pole from Russell
sports.summary: Max Verstappen lapped Marina Bay in 1:31.156 to beat George Russell by 0.120s and keep pole after a yellow-flag probe.
body: The Red Bull driver set his time on softs in SQ3, with Charles Leclerc third for Ferrari. Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris lined up fourth and fifth for McLaren, ahead of Lewis Hamilton and championship leader Kimi Antonelli.
Stewards looked into whether Verstappen had slowed enough for yellow flags but left the result unchanged. The Sprint runs on Saturday, with eight points for the winner.

sports.h3: Russell fastest in practice but faces back-of-grid start
sports.summary: George Russell topped the only practice session in Singapore, but a power unit penalty will drop him to the rear for Sunday's race.
body: Russell's 1:32.274 left him 0.198s clear of Leclerc, with Norris third and Hamilton fourth. Nico Hulkenberg stopped his Audi with a gearbox problem, bringing out a brief Virtual Safety Car.

Mercedes had to fit new engine parts after Russell's late retirement in Malaysia, and the penalty applies only to the Grand Prix. He sits 84 points behind team-mate Antonelli and has reverted to the older car spec used to win in Azerbaijan.

sports.h3: Team New Zealand back on the water in Auckland
sports.summary: The America's Cup defender restarted its AC75 test programme on the Hauraki Gulf, the first team to sail again after the Naples regatta.
body: Tuesday was day 22 of the team's 45 permitted sailing days for 2026. Co-helm Seb Menzies said the session was about recommissioning the boat and crew after time off.
The crew ran tight figure-of-eight drills to rehearse aggressive match-race starts in a choppy easterly. Observers also spotted a new jib sheeting system and test markings on the foil wings.

sports.h3: Luna Rossa damages AC75 hull in Cagliari training
sports.summary: The Italian challenger holed its hull when a Lidar pole broke in a wave crash on its first day back in a month.
body: Luna Rossa returned to the water in Sardinia on 6 October with Peter Burling and Ruggero Tita among the helms. The team logged about 106 minutes of foiling with 24 tacks and 23 gybes.
In the final session the boat slammed into a wave, snapping the Lidar pole onto the starboard hull. Shore crew taped the small hole and the boat sailed on before the day ended.

sports.h3: Oranje guaranteed pot 1 for Euro 2028 qualifying draw
sports.summary: After four Nations League games under Xavi Hernandez, the Netherlands cannot drop out of the top seeding pot for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
body: Two wins over Serbia and draws with Germany and Greece leave Oranje top of their group on eight points. Sunday's 2-1 win in Eindhoven came via a Teun Koopmeiners free kick and a late Joshua Zirkzee tap-in.
With Serbia still on zero, the Dutch are sure of a top-three finish, which secures pot 1 for the draw in Belfast on 6 December. They host Greece in Amsterdam on 13 November and then face Germany.

sports.h3: Dutch women hit Hungary for eight in World Cup play-off
sports.summary: Victoria Pelova and Lineth Beerensteyn both scored hat-tricks in a 0-8 away win, putting the Netherlands on course for the 2027 World Cup.
body: Beerensteyn struck twice inside the opening quarter in Felcsut and Arjan Veurink's side led 0-4 at the break. Damaris Egurrola also scored and Pelova completed her first career hat-trick.
Danielle van de Donk won her 175th cap on the night. The return leg is in Tilburg on Tuesday, with Turkey or Slovenia waiting in the final round.

sports.h3: Unconvincing PSV beat Heerenveen to go top for a day
sports.summary: PSV won 2-0 at home to Heerenveen on Friday and lead the Eredivisie on goal difference ahead of AZ against Feyenoord.
body: Heerenveen had the better first-half chances but Guus Til headed PSV in front after half an hour. A late own goal by Marcus Linday from a Filip Kostic header sealed it.
Peter Bosz's side now have 19 points from eight games, level with AZ. The Alkmaar side visit Feyenoord on Saturday, and either team can reclaim top spot.

sports.h3: Grigalashvili and Kaju reign at judo Worlds in Baku
sports.summary: Tato Grigalashvili won a fourth world title at -81kg and Haruka Kaju defended her -63kg crown as the Baku World Championships passed halfway.
body: Grigalashvili beat home fighter Zelim Tckaev with a waza-ari deep into golden score, and Azerbaijan added a bronze through Omar Rajabli. Kaju's win stretched her run to 40 straight contests.
Japan has dominated the week, with Ai Tsunoda Roustant taking her first senior title at -70kg and Murao winning -90kg on day five. The championships end on 11 October with the mixed team event.

sports.h3: Van Heemst and Van Lieshout miss out on bronze in Baku
sports.summary: Two Dutch judoka lost bronze medal contests this week, leaving the Netherlands still waiting for a first medal in Baku.
body: World Championship debutant Yael van Heemst lost the -78kg bronze bout to Germany's Anna Monta Olekin by ippon inside two minutes on Friday. European champion Joanne van Lieshout fell to Mongolia's Enkhriilen Lkhagvatogoo in the -63kg bronze match on Wednesday.
The Dutch have eleven judoka in Azerbaijan. Simeon Catharina and Michael Korrel both went out at -100kg, and Marit Kamps lost in round two at -78kg.

sports.h3: Jaworski takes double gold at No-Gi Pans
sports.summary: Pawel Jaworski won the medium-heavyweight division and the open class at the IBJJF Pan No-Gi Championship in New Jersey.
body: The fresh ADCC world champion finished his division final with a triangle choke at the Meadowlands Exposition Center. More than 2,300 athletes registered for the 2 to 4 October event.
Jaworski has now won five straight major titles. One more would make him the first winner of the IBJJF No-Gi Grand Slam, with the European No-Gi starting on 28 October.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple sets 'Welcome home' launch for 13 October
consumer-tech.summary: Apple will unveil new smart home products on Tuesday, expected to include a first home hub, a new Apple TV 4K and a HomePod mini refresh.
body: Greg Joswiak teased the date on Thursday, and press invites went out for a hands-on event in Tribeca, New York. Bloomberg says there will also be an online video presentation.

The hub reportedly has a square display of around 6 inches, works on a counter or a wall and runs Siri AI. The Apple TV is said to get a newer chip, 12GB of RAM and Apple's N1 wireless chip, and LG-made accessories such as a doorbell and lock may appear too.

consumer-tech.h3: Touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro tipped for 27 October
consumer-tech.summary: Bloomberg reports a second Apple launch around 27 October with OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros, an M6 iMac and an OLED iPad mini.
body: The 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models are said to use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, a lighter design and a camera cutout. A base 14-inch model with the M6 chip is also expected.
The iPad mini would gain an OLED panel, an A20 Pro chip and water resistance. One rumour says the screen stays at 60Hz.

consumer-tech.h3: iPhone Duo foldable pre-orders open 16 October
consumer-tech.summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone goes on pre-order next Friday and reaches stores on 23 October.
body: The book-style Duo pairs a 5.4-inch outer screen with a 7.6-inch inner display that has only a slight crease. Buyers can start setting up orders from Monday.
Apple Stores will also offer to put the owner's name on the phone's startup screen. It is the headline launch in a busy month for Apple hardware.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple trims iPhone 18 Pro orders on weak demand
consumer-tech.summary: Nikkei Asia says Apple cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro by at least 15 percent after a $100 price rise.
body: The Pro and Pro Max start at $1,199 and $1,299, with Apple blaming AI-driven memory chip costs for price increases across its range. Apple shares fell after the report.
Nikkei also points to Apple's split launch plan as a factor, with the base iPhone 18 moving to spring 2027. Some buyers may also be waiting for the iPhone Duo.

consumer-tech.h3: Microsoft prices Surface Laptop Ultra at $2,599
consumer-tech.summary: Microsoft's 15-inch creator laptop runs on Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark chip and arrives on 16 October.
body: The chip pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores and a Grace CPU with up to 20 cores, plus up to 128GB of unified memory. The laptop has a mini-LED touchscreen and magnetic USB-C charging.
Microsoft is offering up to $1,000 back for traded-in MacBooks. A $5,999 Surface RTX Spark Dev Box aimed at AI developers was also announced.

consumer-tech.h3: Amazon drops Fire OS for Android Alexa Tablets
consumer-tech.summary: Amazon's new aluminium tablets run Android with Google Play and Alexa+, starting at $229.99.
body: The flagship Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs $499.99 with a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 chip and a 120Hz 12-inch screen. A $549.99 version adds a matte glare-reducing display made with Corning.
An 11-inch model starts at $329.99 and an 8.7-inch model at $229.99, with kids editions too. Shipping starts on 14 October in North America and 19 October in parts of Europe.

consumer-tech.h3: Google opens SynthID AI detector to everyone
consumer-tech.summary: Anyone can now upload images, video or audio to Google's SynthID Detector to check for hidden AI watermarks.
body: The tool, first offered to journalists last year, is now live worldwide in English and requires sign-in. It reads SynthID watermarks used by Google, OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao.
Google stresses it is not a general AI detector and cannot tell AI-made from AI-edited files. Apple plans to support SynthID later this year.

consumer-tech.h3: October Pixel update is the last for the Pixel 6
consumer-tech.summary: Google's small October patch reached Pixel 6 through Pixel 11 phones and should be the final update for the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro.
body: The release follows September's larger Android 17 QPR1 drop and lists only three bug fixes. These include a VoIP ringtone distortion fix and a keyboard bug in search fields.
The Pixel 6 and 6 Pro launched in October 2021 and have reached the end of their five-year support window. Google confirmed their end-of-life status in July.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla renames FSD 'Assisted Driving' in Europe
consumer-tech.summary: After Germany called 'Full Self-Driving' misleading, Tesla now sells the system in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving.
body: Germany's transport ministry said the name overstated a system that still needs full driver attention. In return, Berlin will back EU-wide approval, with the speed limit tolerance capped at 10 percent.
The system is approved in eight EU countries including the Netherlands, but an EU vote has slipped to December at the earliest. In the US, Tesla still sells it as Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

consumer-tech.h3: VW ID. Tiguan arrives to replace the ID.4
consumer-tech.summary: Volkswagen's electric Tiguan offers up to 600km WLTP range and goes on sale in Germany from 42,695 euros.
body: The SUV comes with 58kWh or 77kWh batteries and up to 299 PS in all-wheel-drive form. Inside, physical buttons return alongside a 15-inch centre screen and a retro Golf IV gauge mode.
European sales open on 13 October, and the car will replace the ID.4 and ID.5, which sold over 950,000 units combined. North America follows later.

consumer-tech.h3: VW recalls 22,500 ID.4s, advises 80% charge cap
consumer-tech.summary: Volkswagen is recalling 22,524 ID.4 SUVs in the US over a battery fire risk and told owners to limit charging to 80 percent.
body: VW told US regulators that charging some 2023 to 2026 models above 80 percent could trigger thermal propagation. The root cause is still unknown and battery supplier SK Battery America has been asked for details.
There is no fix yet, and owner letters go out on 27 November. It follows an earlier global battery recall of almost 100,000 VW EVs this year.

consumer-tech.summary: BMW's new electric coupe-SUV, the third Neue Klasse model, goes on sale in March 2027.
body: The iX4 50 xDrive has 468 hp and an estimated 428 miles from a 112.2kWh battery, or 828km on WLTP. Its 800V system charges at up to 400kW.
An M60 version with 603 hp follows later. Inside is BMW's panoramic display across the windscreen base, with bidirectional charging as standard.
